reviews.review: It's complex, but not impossible to get into. You can learn just enough to make you dangerous in the tutorials, and set off into the vast amount of content. Even if you have no interest in making your own scenarios or playing multiplayer there is tons of fan scenarios, campaigns, and even whole new game modes to keep it interesting for a long time. If you're looking for a tactical shooter with squad (or solo) based gameplay that is rich, and satisfying look no further.

I see a lot of people complaining about the "No multiplayer servers" and "Game is too hard" reviews on Arma 3 and lemme tell ya from someone who literally never thought they'd get into Arma and only got into it because his friends bought him the game, it has been an absolute blast.

There are some performance issues but it's mainly due to trying to load many assets, models, decals, etc... A lot of the game surprisingly runs very well for an open world military sandbox, even my ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ass gaming laptop can run this game well. There's a lot of DLCs that feature factions, maps, mechanics, weapons, you name it. By far it also has the benefit of the steam workshop, allowing user created content to also spice up the experience with new stuff that constantly refreshes the experience. I will admit however, this game is kinda difficult in terms of learning the controls, however I actually have found the in game popup tips during campaigns and showcases to be extremely helpful in teaching me how to use certain mechanics without holding my hand the entire time. I find multiplayer hard to play usually but for the most part, there are from what I can see communities for these games that utilize both the mods and unmodded scene. For non-dlc owners, you can still play on these servers but you would be forced into having in game popups whenever you use the required DLC items, which I agree, can be annoying but it goes away after a few seconds so I really don't mind it.

I seriously cannot recommend enough if you're a sucker for military games and open world scenarios, it cannot be better than Arma for anyone who doesn't want the over the top graphics game. I'd also wait for when sales are up because usually the DLCs go on sale for really big drops like 50% (As of the current date of writing this review they were 50%).
